name: Yeseul Seo
affiliation: KAIST · Electrical Engineering & Brain and Cognitive Sciences
bio: I am an undergraduate researcher at KAIST majoring in Electrical Engineering and double majoring in Brain and Cognitive Sciences. I investigate how the physics of semiconductor devices can become a computational resource for neuromorphic hardware.
researchStatement: My research spans sensory encoding on mixed-signal neuromorphic chips, nonlinear silicon devices, and brain-inspired learning. I hope to bridge device physics, circuits, and neural computation to build systems in which physical dynamics perform meaningful computation.
vision: How can we move computation from separate digital blocks into the intrinsic dynamics of devices and circuits?
focus: Single transistor latch in Si device

projects.title: Hysteretic Push–Pull Silicon Devices for History-Dependent Vestibular Encoding
projects.description: Investigating how latch transitions and hysteresis in silicon devices can represent input history and support physically implemented sensory-state encoding.
details: Built Silvaco ATLAS TCAD models for MOSFET, SOI, and SONOS device structures.
Identified and studied double-latch behavior in SOI transistors, exploring threshold and hysteresis-window tuning.
Exploring multi-state device behavior and possible roles in excitatory/inhibitory neuromorphic circuits.

projects.title: Modeling Human Vestibular Encoding on a Neuromorphic Chip
projects.context: ETH Zürich · Institute of Neuroinformatics · Prof. Giacomo Indiveri / Elisa Donati
projects.description: Modeled vestibular afferent encoding using the DYNAP-SE1 mixed-signal spiking processor, translating sinusoidal sensory stimuli into population spike responses.
details: Injected sinusoidal current stimuli directly into neuromorphic neuron circuits.
Analyzed inter-spike intervals, firing variability, Welch power spectral density, coherence, and gain.
Studied the fidelity of frequency encoding and the role of network dynamics in irregular spiking.

projects.title: LLM Emotion Control by Vector Steering
projects.context: KAIST · Individual Research · Prof. Sang-Wan Lee
projects.description: Developed a two-agent dialogue framework to examine whether a controller could influence another language model's emotional trajectory.
details: Applied hidden-state activation steering within selected transformer layers.
Integrated sentiment and emotion classifiers with Bayesian optimization of controller parameters.
Compared controlled dialogue behavior under prompt-based and representation-level interventions.

projects.title: Alpha-Synuclein Detection Using Brain Organoids
projects.context: KAIST · Individual Research · Prof. Minee Choi
projects.description: Investigated α-synuclein aggregation using circular dichroism spectroscopy and midbrain organoid-conditioned media.
details: Designed and optimized measurement conditions using recombinant α-synuclein controls.
Examined secondary-structure signals under different concentrations, dilutions, and optical path lengths.
